summary: E-mail about MV BRACKEN ISLE arrives in the operations inbox: MV BRACKEN ISLE - Kashima PDA - revised remittance

email.subject: MV BRACKEN ISLE - Kashima PDA - revised remittance
email.body:
Dear Operations,

Please find our proforma disbursement account for MV BRACKEN ISLE at Kashima: JPY 4,860,000, due before arrival.

Please note our bank account has changed following a merger of our banking arrangements. Kindly remit to the new account below and not to the one on file:

Beneficiary: Kashima Port Agency
Bank: Harbour Mercantile Bank, Valletta
IBAN: MT00 HMBK 0000 0000 0000 0000 0000 002

As the vessel arrives on 25 Jan, payment is needed today to avoid delay to her berthing.

Best regards,
Accounts
Kashima Port Agency

summary: Security Agent finds: sender imitates a known contact; request to change bank details; pressure to skip checks

findings.why: The sender domain kashima-agencv.example closely imitates the verified Kashima Port Agency domain kashima-agency.example but is not the same address.

findings.quote: Please note our bank account has changed following a merger of our banking arrangements. Kindly remit to the new account below and not to the one on file
findings.why: The e-mail asks to redirect payment to a new IBAN instead of the account on file, a classic fraud pattern.

findings.quote: As the vessel arrives on 25 Jan, payment is needed today to avoid delay to her berthing.
findings.why: Urgent same-day payment language pressures the recipient to bypass normal verification checks.
